title: Direct determination of amorphous number density from the reduced pair distribution function
author: Antipas, Karalis

steps.title: Collect diffraction intensity I(Q)
steps.instruction: Perform a diffraction experiment (electron or monochromatic powder X‑ray) and record the scattered intensity I(Q) over a reciprocal‑space range defined by the instrument (Q = 4π sinθ / λ). For the validation example, levitate the sample with compressed air, melt it to 1500 °C using a 100 W CO₂ laser, switch off the laser to quench, and collect high‑energy XRD at λ = 0.20194 Å (61.39 keV) up to Qmax ≈ 21 Å⁻¹ (2θ up to 40°).

steps.title: Correct raw intensity data
steps.instruction: Apply the appropriate corrections to I(Q) for incoherent scattering, multiple scattering, and background contributions. Ensure that after correction the reduced structure factor satisfies F(Qmax)=0 (equivalently S(Qmax)=1).

steps.title: Select Qmax and prepare G(r) range
steps.instruction: Choose a Qmax that fulfills F(Qmax)=0. Compute several G(r) curves using different Qmax cut‑offs and sample each curve at real‑space intervals ≤ the Nyquist rate (π / Qmax). Discard any Qmax that causes noticeable peak‑position shifts or introduces peaks/shoulders that are not present in all curves. The portion of G(r) common to all acceptable Qmax values defines the usable G(r) region for the next step.

steps.title: Fourier‑transform to obtain reduced PDF
steps.instruction: Fourier‑transform the corrected coherent intensity using Eq. (1): G(r)= (2/π) ∫_{Qmin}^{Qmax} F(Q) sin(Qr) dQ, where F(Q)=Q[S(Q)−1] and F(Q)² = I(Q). Perform the transform without window functions (e.g., with an IGOR PRO™ custom subroutine).

steps.title: Calculate rmin from Qmax
steps.instruction: Compute the lower limit of the physically meaningful G(r) range as rmin = 2π / Qmax. For Qmax = 21 Å⁻¹, rmin = 0.3 Å.

steps.title: Define usable G(r) interval
steps.instruction: Set the usable G(r) interval from rmin up to the first coordination peak (the first r where G(r) crosses the x‑axis after the initial peak). In the example, the first coordination peak occurs at 1.65 Å (Si–O bond).

steps.title: Compute G(r)/(4πr) ratio
steps.instruction: Within the usable interval, divide G(r) by 4πr to obtain the ratio G(r)/(4πr).

steps.title: Identify local minima of the ratio
steps.instruction: Using a spreadsheet (see supplementary material), input the G(r) vs. r data (r values in column A starting at A9, G(r) values in column B starting at B9). Calculate rmin from Qmax (cell H1) and the first‑peak position (cell H2). Mark the usable range (column C). Compute the ratio in column D, keep only negative values (column F). For each pair of consecutive points in column F, calculate the tangent (column G) and detect a sign reversal, which flags a local minimum (column H). Record the r position and ratio value for each minimum.

steps.title: Select most negative minimum as density
steps.instruction: From the list of local minima, choose the one with the most negative G(r)/(4πr) value (rd). The amorphous number density is then ρ₀ = –G(rd) / (4π rd). In the validation case the deepest minimum occurs at rd = 0.61 Å, giving ρ₀ = 0.098 atoms Å⁻³.

steps.title: Visualize baseline and assess accuracy
steps.instruction: Plot the baseline –4π ρ₀ r from r = 0 to rd (solid green line) and extend it to higher r (dashed line) to compare with the experimental G(r). For the glass sample the calculated ρ₀ (0.098 atoms Å⁻³) agrees with the independently measured density of 0.088 atoms Å⁻³ (3.54 g cm⁻³) within 15.3 %.
